content: आदि {%a.%} .²1 First, primary, primitive; निदानं त्वादिकारणम् <ls>Ak.</ls> .²2 Chief, first, principal, pre-eminent; <ab>oft.</ab> at the end of <ab>comp.</ab> in this sense; see below. .²3 First in time existing before. .{@-दिः@} .²1 Beginning, commencement (<ab>opp.</ab> अन्त); अप एव ससर्जादौ तासु बीजमवासृजत् <ls>Ms. 1. 8</ls>; <ls>Bg. 3. 41</ls>; अनादि <ab>&c.</ab>; जगदादिरनादिस्त्वम् <ls>Ku. 2. 9</ls>; <ab>oft.</ab> at the end of <ab>comp.</ab> and translated by ‘beginning with’, ‘et caetera’, ‘and others’, ‘and so on’ (of the same nature or kind), ‘such like’; इन्द्रादयो देवाः the gods Indra and others (इन्द्रः आदिर्येषां ते); एवमादि this and the like; भ्वादयो धातवः भू and others, or words beginning with भू, are called roots; <ab>oft.</ab> used by Pāṇini to denote classes or groups of grammatical words; अदादि, दिवादि, स्वादि <ab>&c.</ab> .²2 First part or portion. .²3 A firstling, first-fruits. .²4 Prime cause. .²5 Nearness. .²6 One of the seven parts of Sāma; अथ सप्तविधस्य वाचि सप्तविधं सामोपासीत यत्किंच वाचो हुमिति स हिंकारो यत्प्रेति स प्रस्तावो यदेति स आदिः <ls>Ch. Up. 2. 8. 1</ls>. .{@-पु(पू)रुषः@} .²1 the first or primeval being, the lord of the creation. .²2 Viṣṇu, Kṛṣṇa, or Nārāyaṇa; ते च प्रापुरुदन्वन्तं बुबुधे चादिपूरुषः <ls>R. 10. 6</ls>; तमर्ध्यमर्ध्यादिकयादिपूरुषः <ls>Śi. 1. 14</ls>.
